```{r}
augmented_modeling_function = function(dataset,
                                       target,
                                       k_folds,
                                       model_type,
                                       lower_thresh = 0,
                                       upper_thresh = 251){
  
  pred_concs = NULL
  
  dataset = dataset %>% filter(Conc. > lower_thresh & Conc. < upper_thresh)
  
  gen_rec = recipe(target_vector~., data = dataset) %>% 
    update_role(SampleNum, Conc., new_role = 'id') %>% 
    # step_BoxCox(all_predictors()) %>% 
    step_normalize(all_predictors())

  folds = vfold_cv(dataset, v=10, repeats = 2, strata = target_vector)
  
  if (model_type == 'rbf_svm'){
    mod = svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>% 
    set_mode('classification') %>% 
    set_engine('kernlab')
  }
  
  if (model_type == 'rf'){
    mod = rand_forest(trees = 5000, mtry = tune(), min_n = tune()) %>% 
      set_mode('classification') %>% 
      set_engine('ranger')
  }
  
  resample_results = mod %>% 
    tune_grid(
      gen_rec,
      resamples = folds,
      control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE)
    )
  
  metrics = collect_metrics(resample_results)
  print(metrics)
  return(resample_results)
}

model_results = augmented_modeling_function(labled_augmented_data,
                            'target_vector',
                            k_folds = 5,
                            model_type = 'rf',
                            lower_thresh = 0.9)

collect_predictions(model_results)
show_best(model_results)
show_best(model_results, metric = "accuracy")

unique(collect_predictions(model_results)$.pred_class)
# This is super weird, the class probabilities don't seem to be related to the predicted class,
# meaning that the class with the max probability does not correspond to the predicted class provided.
# If I just take the max probability value and assign class based on that, do we get a different accuracy value?
# RBF_SVM
best_params = show_best(model_results)
best_cost = best_params$cost[[1]]
best_sigma = best_params$rbf_sigma[[1]]

best_param_preds = collect_predictions(model_results) %>% 
  filter(cost == best_cost & rbf_sigma == best_sigma)

# RANDOM FOREST
best_mtry = best_params$mtry[[1]]
best_min_n = best_params$min_n[[1]]

best_param_preds = collect_predictions(model_results) %>% 
  filter(mtry == best_mtry & min_n == best_min_n)

# SAME FOR ALL
best_param_probs = data.frame('Beta' = best_param_preds$.pred_Beta,
                              'Delta' = best_param_preds$.pred_Delta,
                              'Omicron' = best_param_preds$.pred_Omicron,
                              'WT' = best_param_preds$.pred_WT)
best_param_probs$max_prob = apply(best_param_probs, 1, function(x) paste0(names(best_param_probs)[x==max(x)]))
best_param_probs$true_class = best_param_preds$target_vector
best_param_probs

sum(best_param_probs$max_prob == best_param_preds$target_vector)/nrow(best_param_probs)

# Now I could see what the average difference is in probability between the max probability value and the second highest value. Ideally, i would see this
```
